name: Optimize Suite Configuration for Dual Use
consequences: Reconfiguring suites for both research and temporary housing increases facility versatility but requires additional renovation costs and regulatory compliance for mixed-use occupancy. This could delay initial operations if local zoning approvals are delayed.
options: Install modular furniture systems for rapid reconfiguration between research and residential modes
Designate 2 suites as hybrid spaces with retractable privacy partitions and adjustable lighting
Implement temporary partition walls with integrated sensor conduits for scalable expansion
review: Flexibility in suite design risks delayed approvals and increased capital expenditure, leaving unaddressed the long-term maintenance costs of dual-use infrastructure.

name: Adjust Recruitment Criteria for Event Yield
consequences: Lowering the minimum event threshold from 2 to 1 self-reported episodes per month could increase participant numbers but may introduce higher variability in captured data quality and safety risks from overburdened staff.
options: Prioritize recruitment from sleep clinic referrals with documented parasomnia histories
Offer tiered compensation based on event capture frequency to incentivize participation
Screen potential participants using a 10-minute sleep diary protocol before full enrollment
review: Increased recruitment volume creates pressure on staff-to-participant ratios, leaving unaddressed the risk of compromised data integrity from rushed annotations.

name: Enhance Sensor Fusion for Event Detection
consequences: Integrating thermal imaging with existing sensors improves detection accuracy but adds computational overhead and requires additional training for technicians to interpret multi-modal data.
options: Develop a real-time alert system combining audio, motion, and temperature anomalies
Implement machine learning models trained on historical event data to flag potential episodes
Install ceiling-mounted thermal cameras in corridors for non-intrusive activity monitoring
review: Advanced sensor fusion increases data complexity, leaving unaddressed the challenge of maintaining human-in-the-loop oversight for critical decisions.

name: Redesign Shift Schedules for Coverage Gaps
consequences: Implementing staggered 12-hour shifts reduces staff fatigue but creates overlapping coverage periods that may exceed budgeted personnel costs during peak event detection windows.
options: Create 3 rotating 8-hour shifts with 2 technicians per shift for 16-hour daily coverage
Establish a 24/7 on-call system with 3 primary technicians and 2 backup staff
Introduce 6-hour 'micro-shifts' with 4-person rotation cycles for high-event periods
review: Extended coverage hours strain budget limits, leaving unaddressed the potential for critical errors during shift transition periods.

name: Reallocate Budget to High-Impact Areas
consequences: Prioritizing sensor upgrades over staff expansion improves data quality but risks understaffing during peak enrollment periods, potentially delaying event capture timelines.
options: Allocate 20% of year-two budget to sensor calibration and redundancy systems
Invest in automated annotation tools to reduce manual scoring requirements
Redirect funds from control group recruitment to expand parasomnia participant capacity
review: Resource reallocation creates imbalance between technical and human capital, leaving unaddressed the risk of system-wide bottlenecks in data processing.

name: Reconfigure Night Staff Rotation for Cognitive Load Management
consequences: Shifting to 12-hour overnight shifts reduces fatigue-induced annotation errors but increases staffing costs due to higher headcount requirements. The extended shifts may also strain long-term employee retention if not paired with compensatory benefits.
options: Implement 12-hour overnight shifts with mandatory 30-minute break intervals during low-activity periods
Introduce rotating 8-hour night shifts with overlapping 2-hour handover windows for critical event documentation
Deploy dual-tier staffing where 2 full-time technicians handle 8 suites while 1 part-time contractor covers 4 suites during low-risk hours
review: Prioritizing staff cognitive performance risks higher labor costs, leaving the gap of maintaining 24/7 coverage without compromising data annotation accuracy.

name: Integrate Cross-Protocol Data Sharing with Neurology Department
consequences: Sharing de-identified physiological data with University Hospital Bonn's neurology team accelerates biomarker discovery but creates compliance complexity due to dual institutional review board requirements. This could delay data access if not pre-negotiated.
options: Establish a joint data governance committee to standardize metadata formats and access protocols between sleep and neurology departments
Create a tiered data-sharing framework where basic physiological metrics are automatically shared while raw video remains restricted
Develop a pilot collaboration focusing on RBD participants to test interoperability before expanding to NREM parasomnia data
review: Accelerating cross-departmental insights introduces regulatory coordination overhead, leaving the gap of potential data sovereignty disputes unaddressed.

name: Standardize Environmental Variable Logging for Pattern Recognition
consequences: Implementing strict protocols for recording room temperature, humidity, and external noise levels creates a structured dataset for identifying environmental triggers but requires additional technician time for real-time documentation.
options: Install automated environmental sensors with timestamped logs integrated into the primary data acquisition system
Develop a pre-shift checklist requiring staff to document room conditions and participant sleep posture before monitoring begins
Create a secondary database for qualitative environmental notes from night staff to complement quantitative sensor data
review: Enhancing contextual data collection increases operational complexity, leaving the gap of potential data overload without automated analysis tools.

name: Modify Participant Onboarding to Include Sleep Hygiene Education
consequences: Adding sleep hygiene training sessions before admission improves participant compliance with monitoring protocols but extends pre-study preparation time, potentially delaying enrollment timelines.
options: Develop a mandatory 2-hour virtual workshop on sleep environment optimization for all participants before arrival
Create standardized written materials with visual aids for participants to review during the pre-admission phone screening
Implement a pre-residency sleep diary requirement to establish baseline habits and identify compliance risks
review: Improving participant preparedness risks delayed enrollment, leaving the gap of potential throughput reductions unmitigated.

name: Establish Dual-Track Annotation Review Processes
consequences: Creating separate annotation pathways for routine data and flagged events increases inter-rater reliability but requires additional training hours and may create bottlenecks during high-volume data periods.
options: Implement a two-stage review where initial annotations are validated by junior raters before senior raters assess complex cases
Develop a tiered annotation system where basic events use standardized criteria while ambiguous cases trigger consensus meetings
Introduce a randomized double-blind annotation protocol for 20% of all recordings to monitor scorer bias
review: Improving accuracy through layered reviews creates capacity constraints, leaving the gap of delayed data processing unaddressed.

name: Redesign Control Group Participation Incentives
consequences: Offering enhanced compensation for control group participants increases enrollment rates but raises ethical concerns about coercion, particularly for individuals with sleep disturbances seeking alternative care.
options: Provide a tiered compensation structure where control group participants receive 10% higher payment for equivalent participation time
Offer non-monetary incentives such as free sleep consultations with the clinical psychologist for control group participants
Create a hybrid model where control group participants can opt into limited additional monitoring for bonus compensation
review: Attracting control group participants through enhanced rewards risks ethical scrutiny, leaving the gap of potential participant coercion unaddressed.

name: Implement Dynamic Suite Reconfiguration for Event Capture
consequences: Rearranging suite layouts based on participant event patterns improves sensor coverage but requires temporary shutdowns of monitoring equipment during reconfiguration, risking data continuity.
options: Develop a modular furniture system allowing 30-minute reconfigurations during low-activity periods without interrupting sensor networks
Create a rotating suite assignment protocol where participants move between configurations every 72 hours to optimize detection angles
Install adjustable sensor mounts that can be repositioned remotely during monitoring sessions
review: Enhancing spatial adaptability introduces operational disruptions, leaving the gap of potential data loss during reconfiguration unmitigated.

name: Adjust Sensor Placement for Environmental Noise Mitigation
consequences: Relocating acoustic sensors to minimize ambient noise interference improves signal clarity but requires reconfiguring suite layouts, which could disrupt the domestic atmosphere critical for naturalistic behavior. This may also increase installation complexity and maintenance demands.
options: Implement acoustic dampening materials in corridor sensor mounts
Deploy directional microphones to isolate specific activity zones
Integrate machine learning-based noise filtering into real-time data streams
review: Reduced noise interference enhances data quality but increases setup complexity and risks altering participant behavior through visible mitigation measures.

name: Modify Participant Screening for Comorbid Condition Identification
consequences: Adding specialized screening tools for psychiatric or neurological comorbidities strengthens diagnostic specificity but extends pre-admission timelines and may reduce enrollment rates through stricter eligibility criteria.
options: Administer standardized psychiatric symptom checklists during initial interviews
Collaborate with regional psychiatry clinics for concurrent evaluations
Use biomarker assays to detect subclinical neurological abnormalities
review: Enhanced screening improves data validity but creates bottlenecks in participant onboarding and may exclude potential subjects with coexisting conditions.

name: Reconfigure Data Annotation Workflow for Inter-Rater Consistency
consequences: Introducing structured annotation protocols reduces variability in event classification but requires extensive training and may slow down real-time processing during peak activity periods.
options: Establish tiered annotation levels with escalating review thresholds
Implement blinded dual-scoring for ambiguous events
Develop context-aware scoring templates based on participant history
review: Standardized workflows improve reliability but create capacity constraints during high-volume data periods and require ongoing rater calibration efforts.

name: Optimize Staff Training for Emergency Response Protocols
consequences: Enhancing crisis management training improves safety outcomes but diverts time from core research activities and may create dependency on external emergency services during critical incidents.
options: Conduct quarterly simulation drills for seizure and aggression scenarios
Cross-train technicians in basic emergency medical procedures
Partner with local hospitals for rapid response protocol integration
review: Increased preparedness raises training overhead and shifts some responsibility to external entities, potentially complicating incident management authority.

name: Revise Participant Compensation Structure for Retention
consequences: Tying payments to event capture milestones increases motivation but may incentivize participants to manipulate behavior or prolong stays beyond clinical necessity.
options: Offer tiered compensation based on event frequency and duration
Provide additional benefits for completing full stay requirements
Implement flexible scheduling with partial payments for partial participation
review: Performance-based compensation risks altering natural behavior patterns and creates administrative complexity in tracking variable payment structures.

name: Standardize Emergency Response Drills for Staff Familiarity
consequences: Regularized drills improve procedural muscle memory but consume staff time and may create false senses of security if scenarios lack real-world variability.
options: Conduct monthly simulated emergency scenarios with randomized triggers
Require staff to document and debrief after each drill
Incorporate external auditors to evaluate response effectiveness
review: Routine drills enhance preparedness but risk procedural rigidity and may not account for unanticipated crisis configurations.

name: Integrate Cross-Departmental Sleep History Reviews
consequences: Collaborating with neurology and psychiatry departments enriches clinical context but introduces coordination overhead and potential conflicts in diagnostic prioritization.
options: Schedule joint case conferences for complex participant histories
Create shared digital repositories for interdisciplinary review
Develop standardized referral pathways for specialist consultations
review: Interdepartmental collaboration improves diagnostic depth but creates bottlenecks in decision-making and requires ongoing stakeholder alignment.
